title: Gradium Open-Sources Phonon Speech Models Under 50M Parameters
summary:
The Phonon-31m model is now available under an Apache 2.0 license as part of a new suite of on-device voice synthesis tools from Gradium. These text-to-speech models are all under 50 million parameters and are designed for high accuracy across multiple languages, featuring the broadest inference support available to date for this type of on-device speech system.

Running models locally removes the hosting costs and network latency of cloud-based systems, which typically target 100 to 150ms time-to-first-byte in production. a browser demonstration utilizing an optimized WebGPU inference stack shows Phonon achieving a time-to-first-byte of about 10ms. Modal has already deployed a voice agent by integrating these models with its Pipecat framework.

selectedTweets.text:
A new frontier for on-device speech.

We're open-sourcing Phonon, a suite of TTS models under 50m parameters, setting a new standard for naturalness and accuracy across languages, with the broadest inference support to date.

Phonon-31m is available under Apache 2.0.

https://t.co/d3qa9qmnzY🧵

Phonon: a new open, on-device, text-to-speech model from Gradium. It's really good.

Click through, below, and you can test it in your web browser (enabled by an optimized WebGPU inference stack). Go do it,  just to *feel* what it's like when time-to-first-byte is ~10ms.

There are lots of reasons to run agents/models in the cloud. But the trade-offs are cost for hosting and inference, and latency.

We have to work hard to get time-to-first-byte down below 50ms when we're running our models in the cloud. And usually for a text-to-speech model we're aiming for 100-150ms TTFB in production.

Running on-device means you can optimize to run one inference request at a time in a specific hardware and software environment. And the cost is ~$0. (Or, in very demanding applications, the power budget/battery life for the device.)

Open and on-device models make it possible for us to imagine and build new things. I expect to see people post a lot of great Phonon demos over the next few weeks!
